text:
March 3, 2026

Went for my usual Sunday run along the river, about 8 km. Around the 6 km mark I felt a sharp pinch on the outside of my right knee, right where the bone sticks out. I slowed down and walked the last part home. It wasn't swollen, but going down the stairs to the basement hurt more than going up.

I iced it for 15 minutes in the evening and took one ibuprofen. My sister thinks it's IT band trouble because I increased my distance too fast this month. I went from 20 km a week to almost 35 km.

Pain while walking was about a 4 out of 10. Sitting with my leg bent for a long time at work made it stiff, around a 3. I'm going to skip running until Thursday and try the foam roller on the side of my thigh.

March 9, 2026

Follow-up on the right knee. The rest helped. Thursday I tried an easy 3 km and the pinch came back only in the last few hundred meters, more like a 2 out of 10. Foam rolling the outside of my thigh is very painful but the knee feels looser afterwards.

New problem: on Saturday I was carrying the shopping bags up to the third floor and something twinged in my lower back on the left side. Not dramatic, but bending to put on my socks this morning was a 5 out of 10. No pain going down the legs, which the internet says is a good sign.

I slept badly because turning in bed hurt. I put a heat pad on my back for 20 minutes before bed, which felt better than ice. Plan: walk a lot, no heavy lifting, and stop carrying all the bags in one trip.

March 14, 2026

Lower back is better, maybe a 2 out of 10, only when I bend forward first thing in the morning. Walking 30 minutes at lunch every day seems to be the thing that helps most.

Today I cut my left index finger while chopping onions. The knife slipped and went in near the first joint. It bled a lot for about ten minutes. I pressed a clean towel on it and held my hand up. It was deep enough that I wondered about stitches, but the edges closed by themselves, so I used two butterfly strips.

Typing at work was annoying. Pain was a 3, mostly when I bumped the finger. I'll change the bandage every day and watch for redness. My last tetanus shot was in 2021, so I think I'm fine.

March 22, 2026

The finger cut is healing well. No redness, no pus, just a pink line and a little numbness on the tip. The nurse at the pharmacy said the numbness can last a few weeks if a small nerve was touched.

I started running again this week: 5 km on Tuesday and 6 km on Saturday, both slow. The right knee didn't hurt at all during the runs. I felt it a tiny bit after Saturday's run when I stood up from the couch, maybe a 1 out of 10.

Something I noticed: my knee seems to hurt more when I run on the sloped path by the river and less on the flat track. I'll stick to the track for now. I also bought new running shoes because my old ones had more than 900 km on them.

April 2, 2026

Bad day. I rolled my left ankle stepping off the curb outside the bakery. It turned inward and I heard a small pop. I couldn't put weight on it for the first few minutes. Pain was an 8 out of 10 at the start, then it settled to about a 6.

By the evening it was swollen on the outside, below the ankle bone, and there was some bruising starting. I did rest, ice, compression and kept it up on two pillows. I could walk a little by the evening, limping, so I don't think it's broken, but I booked a doctor's appointment for Monday to be sure.

The knee and back are completely fine, so of course it's the ankle now. No running for a while.

April 6, 2026

Saw Dr. Lambert about the ankle. She pressed on the bones and said no X-ray was needed because I could take four steps and the bones weren't tender. Her diagnosis: a grade 1 to 2 sprain of the ligament on the outside of the ankle.

Her advice: walk on it as much as the pain allows, use the ankle brace for two weeks, and start balance exercises once the swelling goes down, like standing on one leg while brushing my teeth. She said most people go back to running in four to six weeks, and that skipping the balance work is the main reason sprains come back.

The swelling is less today, and pain while walking is about a 4. The bruise has spread down to my heel and is purple and yellow, which she said is normal.

April 15, 2026

Ankle update. I can walk normally now with the brace and almost normally without it. Pain about a 2 out of 10, more at the end of the day. One-leg standing on the left side is much harder than on the right: I lose balance after about 15 seconds on the left versus a full minute on the right.

I started cycling on the stationary bike at the gym because it doesn't hurt the ankle. 20 minutes, easy. The knee feels great on the bike.

I had a headache most of the afternoon, behind the eyes. I think it was from staring at the screen without breaks and drinking only coffee. Two glasses of water and a walk outside made it go away. Not an injury, just writing it down.

April 28, 2026

First run since the sprain: 3 km on the flat track, brace on. The ankle held up fine, maybe a 1 out of 10 afterwards. The balance exercises are paying off. I can stand on the left leg for 45 seconds now.

At the gym I tried the shoulder press machine for the first time in months and felt a pinch at the front of my right shoulder at the top of the movement. I stopped right away. It doesn't hurt at rest, only when I lift my arm above my head, about a 3. Reaching for the top shelf in the kitchen is the worst.

I think I used too much weight. Next time I'll start much lighter. I'm not too worried, but I'll keep an eye on it because my dad had shoulder problems.

May 10, 2026

The right shoulder hasn't really improved in almost two weeks. Overhead movements still hurt, about a 3 or 4, and now it also aches at night if I sleep on that side. I wake up around 3 a.m. and have to turn over.

I booked a physiotherapist. Until then I'm avoiding anything overhead and doing gentle arm circles. Running is going well: 15 km this week with no ankle or knee pain at all.

Side note: on May 7 I bumped my head on the open kitchen cabinet door. Small bump on the forehead, no dizziness, no nausea, no headache afterwards. It was just embarrassing. The bump was gone after two days.

May 19, 2026

First physio session for the shoulder with Marco. He tested my strength and range of motion and said it looks like irritation of the rotator cuff tendons, probably from the shoulder press with too much weight and from bad posture at my desk. He said it's common and usually gets better in six to eight weeks with the right exercises.

Homework: three times a day, external rotation with a light resistance band, 3 sets of 12, and wall slides. No overhead lifting for now, no pressing at the gym. He also told me to raise my monitor so I stop leaning forward.

Pain during the session got up to a 5 when he moved my arm sideways, but afterwards it felt better than before I went in.

June 1, 2026

Shoulder is getting better with the band exercises. Night pain is mostly gone, and overhead reaching is now about a 2. Marco added a new exercise, side-lying arm raises with a 1 kg weight.

I had a fall on my bike on May 30. The road was wet and I braked too hard going around a corner. I landed on my left side. Scrapes on my left forearm and left hip, a lot of road rash but nothing deep. I cleaned it with water and soap at home, which stung like crazy, and covered the forearm because it kept sticking to my sleeve.

The hip is bruised and sore when I lie on it, about a 4. The helmet has a scratch, so I'm glad I was wearing it. My wrist hurt a bit right after the fall, but it was fine by the evening.

June 12, 2026

The road rash on my forearm has almost healed, just pink new skin. The hip bruise is now a big green and yellow patch but only hurts when I press on it, a 1 out of 10.

The right shoulder had a setback. I helped my friend move a sofa on June 10, and lifting it above my head to get it through the door was a bad idea. The night pain came back, a 4 out of 10, and the arm feels weak when I lift it sideways.

I messaged Marco and he said not to panic: go back to the easier exercises for a week and use ice after them. Lesson learned: no helping people move furniture until the shoulder is fully better.

June 25, 2026

Shoulder recovered from the sofa setback. I'm back at the level I was before, overhead reaching about a 1 to 2.

Running is going really well. I did a 10 km race on June 21 in 54 minutes, my best time ever. No knee pain during the race. The left ankle felt a bit tired in the last kilometer but did not hurt.

The day after the race both calves were very tight and sore, like a 5 out of 10 going down stairs. I think it's normal muscle soreness from racing hard. It was much better by June 24 after some easy walking and stretching. I also had a blister on my right big toe from the new racing socks, which I popped and covered.

July 8, 2026

Hot week. I went hiking in the mountains on July 5 and 6. On the first day the trail was steep and rocky, and going downhill for two hours made the front of both knees ache, a 3 out of 10. It wasn't the old pinch on the outside of the right knee, more of a general tired ache, and it went away by the next morning.

On the second day I got stung by a wasp on my right hand while eating lunch. It swelled up a lot, the whole back of the hand, and was itchy and hot for two days. No trouble breathing or anything scary. An antihistamine and a cold pack helped.

I also got a bad sunburn on the back of my neck because I forgot to put sunscreen there. It was red and painful for three days, around a 3 out of 10.

July 20, 2026

Last physio session with Marco. He said the shoulder is fully strong again and I can go back to the shoulder press, starting at half the weight I used in April and adding a little each week. I should keep doing the band exercises twice a week to prevent it coming back.

The right knee has been pain-free for months now. The ankle too, though I still do the one-leg balance exercise while brushing my teeth because it's become a habit.

Today I stubbed my left little toe on the bed frame at night. Pain was an intense 7 for about a minute, then a 3. It's a bit purple tonight. I taped it to the toe next to it, which is what my mom always told me to do.

August 4, 2026

The little toe was sore for about a week but it's fine now. I think it was just bruised, not broken, because I could walk on it the whole time.

I started a new job with a lot more sitting. After the first two weeks my neck and the top of my shoulders feel stiff by the end of the day, about a 3. There's also a tension headache some afternoons. I set up the desk properly: monitor at eye level, feet flat on the floor, and a timer to stand up every 45 minutes.

Also my lower back came back a little, the same left side as in March, a 2 out of 10 after long meetings. It goes away when I walk. I think sitting all day is the problem, not lifting this time.

August 23, 2026

Summary of the summer, since I'm going on holiday tomorrow and won't write for a while.

Things that are fully healed: right knee, left ankle sprain, finger cut, bike road rash, hip bruise, wasp sting, sunburn, little toe. The right shoulder is about 95 percent better, and I'm pressing again with light weights without pain.

Things still bothering me: neck stiffness from the new desk job, about a 2 now that I take breaks, and the lower back on the left side after long meetings, a 2. The standing timer helps both a lot.

Goals for autumn: run a half marathon in October, keep doing the shoulder band exercises twice a week, and keep the balance exercise habit for the ankle.

September 15, 2026

Back from holiday. On September 2 I slipped on a wet rock at the beach and caught myself with my right hand. My right wrist has hurt ever since, on the thumb side, especially when I twist a jar lid or push myself up from a chair, about a 4 out of 10.

Because it's been almost two weeks and still hurts, I went to the walk-in clinic today. The doctor was worried because the pain is in the spot called the anatomical snuffbox, where a small bone called the scaphoid can break without showing on the first X-ray. The X-ray today looked normal, but she put me in a thumb splint anyway and wants a second X-ray in ten days.

Typing with the splint is slow. Running is allowed, but no push-ups or anything that puts weight on the wrist.

September 26, 2026

Second wrist X-ray: still no fracture, so the doctor thinks it's a ligament sprain. I can take the splint off, but I should avoid heavy loading for another two weeks and slowly start wrist circles and squeezing a soft ball. Pain is down to a 2 out of 10.

Half marathon training is going OK. I did 16 km last Sunday. My right knee was fine, but I felt the old pinch on the outside of the right knee again at around 14 km, a 2 out of 10. Same spot as in March. I think it's the long distance again, so I'll add hip strengthening exercises and foam rolling like last time.

The neck and lower back have been fine since I got a standing desk at work two weeks ago.

October 19, 2026

I ran the half marathon today in 2 hours 1 minute. I'm a bit disappointed I didn't get under two hours, but happy I finished without walking.

The right knee started to pinch at around 17 km and got up to a 4 out of 10 by the finish. The left ankle and right wrist were both totally fine. My right shoulder didn't bother me at all.

After the race I had a big blister under my left foot and very sore thighs, a 6 out of 10 going down stairs. I'm taking a full week off running. If the knee pinch is still there next week, I'll go back to the physio, because it has now come back three times with long runs.
